assertions.name: A1_coxeter_is_an_nth_root_of_the_full_twist
assertions.source: Delta^2 = c_n^n acts as a scalar on every block at n=3,4,5

assertions.name: A4_achievable_twists_are_rational
assertions.source: 13 distinct t in (0,1) for n <= 12, all rational, hence all ratios rational

assertions.name: A5_qcd_colour_ratio_is_exactly_available
assertions.source: t = 1/3 realised at n = 12, giving ratio exactly 2

assertions.name: A6_nuclear_ratio_is_not_available
assertions.source: nearest t = 10/11 gives ratio 21, needing a 105.9 keV virtual state vs ~66

description: Answers the question qou-vlrq left open: can the substrate produce the fractional framing twist that the det T = -1 hull exit requires? YES, and with no new ingredient. The Coxeter element c_n = s_1...s_(n-1) satisfies c_n^n = Delta^2, the full twist and centre generator of B_n, so it is a genuine n-th root of a twist; Delta^2 is verified to act as a scalar on every block at n=3,4,5, and the block magnitude of c_n is exactly q^(2 c(lambda)/n) with c(lambda) the content sum (worst deviation 1e-8 or better). Twist exponents are therefore rational with denominator dividing n. Since 2c(lambda) is always even it is divisible by n at n=3 and n=4, so n = 5 is the FIRST strand count carrying a fractional twist (t = 4/5 at (3,2) and (2,2,1)) — the arc had been working at n=2 and n=3 where the fractional part vanishes. Contrast the ribbon twist read directly off the content sum, theta = q^(2c), which is an integer power at every n: the fractionality lives in taking a ROOT of the twist, not in the twist. Exhaustive enumeration over partitions with n <= 12 gives 13 distinct t in (0,1), and every achievable channel ratio (1+t)/(1-t) is rational. The two targets come out opposite. QCD's colour ratio 2 — the exact 3bar/6 colour-factor ratio from 3(x)3 — is hit EXACTLY at t = 1/3, realised at n=12 by (4,4,2,1,1) and (4,3,3,2), with nothing fitted on either side. The nuclear 33.7055 needs t = 0.942372 and is NOT in the set; the nearest is 10/11 giving 21, which would require the np 1S0 virtual state at 105.9 keV against the accepted ~66 keV, a 60% shift far outside its uncertainty. The 1/3 coincidence is reported with its significance assessed downward: 13 rationals is not a sparse set and 1/3 is not an unlikely member.

mechanism.relation: c_n^n = Delta^2 (full twist, centre of B_n)

caveats: THE t = 1/3 HIT IS SUGGESTIVE, NOT EVIDENTIAL. It is exact and nothing is fitted on either side, which is worth recording. But the achievable set for n <= 12 has thirteen members and 1/3 is not an unlikely element of a set of small-denominator rationals. No significance test is offered and none should be inferred. What is established without qualification is the ASYMMETRY: a rational set can meet an exact group-theoretic target and cannot meet a dynamical one.

THIS SHOWS THE TWIST EXISTS, NOT THAT THE CONSTRUCTION USES IT. The Coxeter element is an n-th root of the full twist and its block magnitudes are fractional powers of q from n=5. Nothing here attaches it to a bond, recomputes a binding energy, or exhibits any reason the physical bond SHOULD carry c_n rather than any other element. The hull exit needs a framing scalar; this demonstrates the substrate contains operators supplying fractional ones.

The n <= 12 enumeration is exhaustive over partitions but is a CUTOFF. Larger n supply further rationals with larger denominators, so 'not in the set' for the nuclear target is a statement about n <= 12, not a theorem. The substantive point survives the cutoff: the set is rational at every n while the nuclear target is a measured ratio of two shallow binding energies.

The nuclear target inherits qou-m896's least certain input, the np 1S0 virtual state at ~66 keV. That is why A6 is phrased as the shift REQUIRED (to 105.9 keV, 60%) rather than as a bare mismatch — the conclusion is robust precisely because the needed shift is far outside the uncertainty on that number.
